l: darkness, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 19
s: Darkness characterizes the land and the people who dwell in the land of the shadow of death. The people in darkness see a great light, but the land is later darkened through the wrath of the Lord of Hosts.

l: light, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 19
s: Light shines upon the people who walk in darkness and dwell in the land of the shadow of death. The Lord’s word lights upon Israel.

l: The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 20
s: The Lord God of Hosts condemns those who make unrighteous decrees and declares that the Assyrian will be used against a hypocritical nation and the people of his wrath. The Assyrian intends to destroy many nations and boasts of conquering Calno, Carchemish, Hamath, Arpad, Samaria, and Damascus, but the Lord will punish his proud heart after completing his work upon Mount Zion and Jerusalem. The Lord will burn the Assyrian's glory, while a remnant of Israel and the house of Jacob will return and rely upon the Holy One of Israel. The Lord promises that the Assyrian's burden and yoke will be removed, and that the Lord of Hosts will humble the high and haughty.

l: Holy One of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 20
s: The Lord God of Hosts condemns unjust rulers, sends the Assyrian against a hypocritical nation, and promises to punish the Assyrian's proud heart. He will make a consumption in all the land, remove the Assyrian's burden and yoke, and cut down the high and haughty.

l: Assyrian, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 20
s: The Assyrian is the rod of the Lord's anger and is sent to take spoil, prey, and tread people down. He intends to destroy and cut off many nations, boasts of his conquests, and is later threatened with leanness, burning, and the removal of his burden and yoke.

l: Israel, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 20
s: Israel is described as having people who may be as numerous as the sand of the sea, yet only a remnant will return. The remnant of Israel will no longer rely on the one who smote them but will rely on the Lord in truth.

l: remnant of the house of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 20
s: The remnant of Israel will return and will no longer stay upon him that smote them. It will stay upon the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.

l: house of Jacob, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 20
s: Those escaped of the house of Jacob will no longer rely on him that smote them but will rely upon the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, in truth.

l: Samaria, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 20
s: Samaria is named among the kingdoms and cities conquered by the Assyrian. The Assyrian says he will do to Jerusalem and its idols as he did to Samaria and its idols.

l: Mount Zion, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 20
s: The Lord will perform his whole work upon Mount Zion before punishing the fruit of the stout heart of the king of Assyria.

l: Jerusalem, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 20
s: Jerusalem is included in the Lord's work, and the Lord will punish the king of Assyria after that work is completed. The Assyrian threatens to do to Jerusalem and its idols as he did to Samaria and its idols, and the Assyrian later shakes his hand against the hill of Jerusalem.

l: Assyria, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 20
s: Assyria is not named in this unit.

l: Assyrian army, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 20
s: The Assyrian army is not named in this unit.

l: anger, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 20
s: The Lord's anger is not turned away, and his hand remains stretched out. His anger is described as being used in sending the Assyrian against a hypocritical nation, and it will cease in a little while when the Assyrian is destroyed.

l: the Lord's work upon Mount Zion and Jerusalem, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 20
s: The Lord will perform his whole work upon Mount Zion and upon Jerusalem before punishing the fruit of the stout heart of the king of Assyria.

l: punishment of Assyria, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 20
s: The Lord will punish the fruit of the stout heart of the king of Assyria and the glory of his high looks. The Lord will send leanness among his fat ones and kindle a burning under his glory.

l: rod of God's anger, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 20
s: The Assyrian is called the rod of the Lord's anger, and the staff in the Assyrian's hand is described as the Lord's indignation.

l: remnant's return, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 20
s: The remnant of Israel and the remnant of Jacob will return to the mighty God. Though Israel is as the sand of the sea, a remnant will return as the consumption decreed overflows with righteousness.

l: consumption, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 20
s: The consumption decreed will overflow with righteousness. The Lord God of Hosts will make a consumption that is determined in all the land.

l: burden, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 20
s: In that day the Assyrian's burden will be taken away from Israel's shoulder.

l: yoke, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 20
s: In that day the Assyrian's yoke will be taken from Israel's neck and will be destroyed because of the anointing.

l: The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: The unit concerns a rod and branch from Jesse upon whom the Spirit of the Lord rests, giving wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, and fear of the Lord. He judges with righteousness and equity, and under his reign animals dwell peacefully while the earth is full of the knowledge of the Lord. The Lord sets his hand to recover the remnant of his people, gathers Israel and Judah, and sets up an ensign for the nations. A highway is made for the remnant from Assyria, like Israel’s exodus from Egypt.

l: Jesse, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: A rod comes out of Jesse’s stem, and a branch grows from his roots.

l: the rod and branch from Jesse, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: The rod and branch receive the Spirit of the Lord, including wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, and fear of the Lord. They judge the poor with righteousness, reprove the meek with equity, smite the earth with the rod of their mouth, and slay the wicked with the breath of their lips.

l: the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: The Lord’s Spirit rests upon the rod and branch from Jesse. In that day, the Lord sets his hand again to recover the remnant of his people and sets up an ensign for the nations.

l: the Spirit of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: The Spirit of the Lord rests upon the rod and branch from Jesse and gives the spirit of wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, and fear of the Lord.

l: knowledge of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: The earth becomes full of the knowledge of the Lord as the waters cover the sea.

l: fear of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: The rod and branch from Jesse have quick understanding in the fear of the Lord and do not judge by sight or hearing.

l: righteousness, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: Righteousness is the girdle of the rod and branch from Jesse’s loins. The rod and branch judge the poor with righteousness.

l: the earth, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: The rod and branch smite the earth with the rod of their mouth. The earth becomes full of the knowledge of the Lord.

l: the holy mountain, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: No one hurts or destroys in all the Lord’s holy mountain.

l: Gentiles, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: The Gentiles seek the root of Jesse, whose rest is glorious.

l: covenant people of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: The Lord sets his hand again to recover the remnant of his people left among various lands and regions. A highway is made for the remnant from Assyria.

l: Assyria, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: The remnant of the Lord’s people is recovered from Assyria. A highway is made for the remnant from Assyria.

l: Egypt, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: The remnant of the Lord’s people is recovered from Egypt. The Lord destroys the tongue of the Egyptian sea and makes men go over dry shod.

l: nations, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: The Lord sets up an ensign for the nations.

l: Israel, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: The outcasts of Israel are assembled. Israel is mentioned as having come up out of Egypt, and a highway is made for the remnant like Israel’s exodus.

l: Judah, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: The dispersed of Judah are gathered from the four corners of the earth. Judah and Ephraim no longer envy or vex one another, and Judah lays its hand upon Edom and Moab.

l: Ephraim, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: The envy of Ephraim departs, and Ephraim no longer envies Judah. Ephraim and Judah are no longer adversaries.

l: the outcasts of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: The Lord assembles the outcasts of Israel.

l: the dispersed of Judah, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: The Lord gathers the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.

l: the highway, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: A highway is made for the remnant of the Lord’s people from Assyria, like the way Israel came up out of Egypt.

l: the recovery of the remnant, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: The Lord sets his hand again the second time to recover the remnant of his people from Assyria, Egypt, Pathros, Cush, Elam, Shinar, Hamath, and the islands of the sea.

l: the gathering of Israel and Judah, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: The Lord assembles the outcasts of Israel and gathers the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.

l: the exodus from Egypt, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 21
s: Israel’s coming up out of the land of Egypt is used as the comparison for the highway made for the remnant from Assyria.

l: The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 22
s: The speaker praises the Lord because divine anger has turned away and comfort has come. God is declared to be salvation, strength, and song, and people draw water with joy from the wells of salvation. The people are told to praise the Lord, call on his name, declare his doings, and sing because he has done excellent things. The inhabitant of Zion is told to cry out and shout because the Holy One of Israel is in its midst.

l: Jesus Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 22
s: Lord JEHOVAH is declared to be the speaker's strength and song. He turns away anger, provides comfort, and is praised for doing excellent things.

l: salvation, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 22
s: Salvation is identified with God, and people trust in it without fear. People draw water with joy from the wells of salvation.

l: praise, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 22
s: Praise is offered to the Lord because his anger has turned away and he has comforted the speaker. People are told to praise the Lord, call upon his name, and declare his doings.

l: Zion, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 22
s: The inhabitant of Zion is told to cry out and shout. The Holy One of Israel is said to be in Zion's midst.

l: The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 23
s: The unit concerns Babylon and the coming day of the Lord, when the Lord of Hosts gathers armies from distant nations against it. The whole land will be laid desolate, the wicked will be punished, and Babylon will become uninhabited like Sodom and Gomorrah. The Medes will attack Babylon without regard for silver or gold. The Lord of Hosts will shake the heavens and the earth, while a man will become more precious than fine gold.

l: Babylon, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 23
s: Babylon, described as the glory of kingdoms and the beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency, will be overthrown like Sodom and Gomorrah. It will become desolate and uninhabited, with wild beasts and doleful creatures dwelling in its houses.

l: Lord of Hosts, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 23
s: The Lord of Hosts musters the hosts of battle and sends the weapons of his indignation to destroy the whole land. In the day of his fierce anger, he shakes the heavens and causes the earth to move from its place.

l: kingdoms of nations, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 23
s: The kingdoms of nations gather together in a tumultuous multitude in the mountains. They come from a far country, from the end of heaven, for battle.

l: whole land, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 23
s: The whole land is targeted for destruction by the weapons of the Lord’s indignation. It will be laid desolate.

l: day of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 23
s: The day of the Lord comes as a destruction from the Almighty, with wrath and fierce anger. It brings fear, sorrow, darkness, punishment, and desolation.

l: the wicked, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 23
s: The wicked are punished for their iniquity, and the sinners are destroyed from the land. Those joined to the wicked fall by the sword, and the wicked ultimately perish.

l: man, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 23
s: A man will become more precious than fine gold, even than the golden wedge of Ophir.

l: the earth, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 23
s: The earth will remove from its place when the Lord of Hosts shakes the heavens in the day of his fierce anger.

l: Medes, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 23
s: The Medes are stirred up against Babylon. They do not regard silver and gold, and their bows dash young men to pieces without pity for children.

l: The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 24
s: The Lord will have mercy on Jacob, choose Israel, return them to their lands of promise, and give them rest from sorrow, fear, and bondage. The king of Babylon, identified as Lucifer, is brought down from heaven to hell after exalting himself above the Most High and oppressing nations. Babylon will be swept with destruction, while the Lord will overthrow the Assyrian and establish safety for the poor of his people in Zion. The Lord’s purpose over the whole earth and all nations will stand.

l: the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 24
s: The Lord will have mercy on Jacob, choose Israel, set them in their own land, and give them rest from sorrow, fear, and bondage. He will break the power of the wicked, rise against Babylon, overthrow the Assyrian, and establish Zion as a refuge for the poor of his people.

l: Jacob, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 24
s: Jacob will be shown mercy, and the house of Jacob will be joined by strangers. Jacob’s people will be brought to their place and will rule over those who oppressed them.

l: Israel, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 24
s: Israel will be chosen by the Lord and set in its own land. The house of Israel will possess those who had held them captive.

l: house of Jacob, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 24
s: The house of Jacob will be joined by strangers who cleave to it. It will possess the people who had possessed it and rule over its oppressors.

l: lands of promise, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 24
s: The people will return to their lands of promise from far away, even unto the ends of the earth.

l: the oppressor, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 24
s: The oppressors of the people will be ruled over by those whom they had oppressed.

l: rest, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 24
s: The Lord will give rest from sorrow, fear, and the hard bondage in which the people were made to serve. The whole earth will also be at rest and quiet after the oppressor ceases.

l: king of Babylon, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 24
s: The king of Babylon will be the subject of a proverb because the oppressor and the golden city have ceased. He will be brought down to hell, cast out like an abominable branch, and denied burial because he destroyed his land and slew his people.

l: Babylon, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 24
s: Babylon will have its name, remnant, son, and nephew cut off by the Lord. It will become a possession for the bittern and pools of water and will be swept with the besom of destruction.

l: nations, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 24
s: The nations will be ruled in anger by the oppressor, but their kings will be raised from their thrones in hell to meet him. Messengers of the nations will receive the answer that the Lord has founded Zion and that the poor of his people will trust in it.

l: the earth, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 24
s: The whole earth will be at rest and quiet and will break forth into singing. The Lord’s purpose is purposed upon the whole earth, and his hand is stretched out upon all nations.

l: hell, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 24
s: Hell from beneath will be moved to meet the king of Babylon at his coming. It will stir up the dead and raise the kings of the nations from their thrones.

l: Lucifer, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 24
s: Lucifer will fall from heaven and be cut down to the ground after weakening the nations. He will be brought down to hell because he sought to ascend above the stars of God and be like the Most High.

l: heaven, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 24
s: Lucifer will fall from heaven after seeking to ascend into it and exalt his throne above the stars of God.

l: man (Lucifer), The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 24
s: Those who see him will consider him and ask whether he is the man who made the earth tremble, shook kingdoms, made the world a wilderness, destroyed cities, and did not open the house of his prisoners.

l: world, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 24
s: The world will be made as a wilderness by the man who oppressed it and destroyed its cities.

l: Assyrian, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 24
s: The Lord will bring the Assyrian into his land and tread him underfoot upon the mountains. Then the yoke and burden of the Assyrian will depart from the people.

l: Palestina, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 24
s: Palestina is warned not to rejoice because the rod of the one who smote it is broken. It will howl and cry because smoke will come from the north, and its root will be killed with famine.

l: the poor, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 24
s: The first-born of the poor will feed, and the needy will lie down in safety. The poor of the Lord’s people will trust in Zion.

l: Zion, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 24
s: The Lord has founded Zion, and the poor of his people will trust in it.

l: purpose of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 24
s: The Lord’s purpose over the whole earth will come to pass and cannot be disannulled. His stretched-out hand cannot be turned back.

l: The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: Nephi explains that Isaiah’s words are difficult for many because they do not know the manner of prophesying among the Jews, but they are plain to those filled with the spirit of prophecy. He prophesies that the Jews will be destroyed, restored to Jerusalem, reject and crucify Jesus Christ, and later be scattered until they believe in Christ. He teaches that Jesus Christ is the only name by which people can be saved, that the Lord will restore his people through a marvelous work and a wonder, and that Nephi’s writings will be preserved to judge and convince future generations. Nephi’s people believe in Christ, keep the law of Moses until it is fulfilled, and teach their children to seek remission of sins through Christ.

l: Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: Nephi explains Isaiah’s words and gives his own plain prophecy concerning the Jews, Jesus Christ, the restoration of Israel, and the preservation of his writings. He teaches his people to believe in Christ, be reconciled to God, and look to Christ for remission of sins.

l: Isaiah, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: Isaiah spoke many things that were hard for Nephi’s people to understand because they did not know the manner of prophesying among the Jews. Nephi delights in Isaiah’s words and says they will be understood and be of great worth in the last days.

l: Jews, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: The Jews are repeatedly destroyed because of iniquity, carried captive into Babylon, restored to Jerusalem, and later scattered among all nations. They reject and crucify Jesus Christ, but will eventually believe in Christ, worship the Father in his name, and accept these things.

l: Israel, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: Israel is brought out of Egypt, and the Lord promises to restore his people from their lost and fallen state. The writings preserved by Nephi are connected to the promise that Joseph’s seed should never perish while the earth stands.

l: Holy One of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: God brings judgments upon all nations according to his word and reveals them through prophets. He promises the preservation of Nephi’s writings, restores his people, and provides salvation through Jesus Christ.

l: Jesus Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: Jesus Christ is the Only Begotten of the Father and the only name given under heaven whereby people can be saved. He is rejected by the Jews, rises from the dead, and is the source of grace, reconciliation, and remission of sins.

l: people (Nephi's people), The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: Nephi’s people have difficulty understanding the manner of the Jews, and Nephi teaches them plainly so they cannot err. They believe in Christ, keep the law of Moses because of the commandments, and teach their children about Christ.

l: nations, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: The nations receive judgments from God according to his word and possess the writings preserved by Nephi. Other nations scourge and scatter the Jews for many generations.

l: Jerusalem, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: Jerusalem is the land from which Nephi’s father departed and to which the Jews return after captivity. After Jesus Christ rises from the dead, Jerusalem is destroyed again.

l: words of Isaiah, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: The words of Isaiah concern judgments and future events and are difficult for some to understand. They are plain to those filled with the spirit of prophecy and will be of great worth to Nephi’s people in the last days.

l: scriptures written by Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: Nephi’s writings are promised to be kept, preserved, and handed down from generation to generation as long as the earth stands. They will judge the nations that possess them and convince people of the true Messiah.

l: prophecy, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: Prophecy reveals the destruction and restoration of the Jews, the coming and rejection of Jesus Christ, and the preservation of Nephi’s writings. Nephi says his prophecy is plain and that no man can err in understanding it.

l: spirit of prophecy, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: The spirit of prophecy makes the words of Isaiah plain to those who possess it. Nephi speaks and prophesies according to the spirit in him.

l: judgments of God, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: The judgments of God come upon all nations according to his word. Nephi teaches that the Jews’ destructions were foretold by the prophets because of their iniquities.

l: destruction of Jerusalem, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: Jerusalem is destroyed after the Jews reject and crucify Jesus Christ. Nephi says woe comes upon those who fight against God and the people of his church.

l: scattering and captivity, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: After Jerusalem is destroyed again, the Jews are scattered among all nations. They are scourged by other nations for many generations until they are persuaded to believe in Christ.

l: rejection of Jesus Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: The Jews reject Jesus Christ because of their iniquities, hardness of heart, and stiffness of necks. Nephi teaches that rejecting Christ also denies the prophets and the law.

l: the crucifixion of Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: The Jews crucify Jesus Christ, and he is laid in a sepulchre for three days. His crucifixion occurs before his resurrection and manifestation to those who believe in his name.

l: resurrection of Jesus Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: Jesus Christ rises from the dead after three days with healing in his wings. Those who believe in his name are saved in the kingdom of God.

l: the atonement, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: The atonement of Jesus Christ is infinite for all mankind. The Jews will eventually be persuaded to believe in Christ and the atonement.

l: restoration of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: The Lord sets his hand again to restore his people from their lost and fallen state. This restoration includes bringing forth words to convince them of the true Messiah.

l: the work of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: The Lord proceeds to do a marvelous work and a wonder among the children of men as part of restoring his people.

l: law of Moses, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: Nephi’s people keep the law of Moses while looking forward with steadfastness to Christ. The law becomes dead to them through Christ, but they continue keeping it because of the commandments until it is fulfilled.

l: grace of God, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: Nephi’s people know that they are saved by grace after all they can do. Their teaching about grace is connected to belief in Christ and reconciliation with God.

l: faith, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: Nephi’s people are made alive in Christ because of their faith, even while they keep the law of Moses. Faith in Christ is central to their hope of salvation.

l: remission of sins, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 25
s: Nephi and his people talk, rejoice, preach, prophesy, and write about Christ so their children will know where to look for a remission of their sins.

l: The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 26
s: Nephi teaches that after Christ rises from the dead, he will show himself to his people, and his words will be their law. He prophesies of wars, Christ’s birth, death, and resurrection, the destruction of the wicked, and the preservation of the righteous who heed the prophets and look to Christ. He describes the last days, including the fall of Nephi’s people, the Gentiles’ pride and churches, secret combinations, and the emergence of written words from those destroyed. He also teaches that God offers salvation and goodness freely to all, forbids priestcraft and iniquity, and commands charity.

l: Jesus Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 26
s: Jesus Christ will rise from the dead, show himself to Nephi’s people, and speak the law they are to follow. He will manifest himself to all who believe in him through the power of the Holy Ghost and will heal the righteous.

l: Lord God, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 26
s: God will bring forth words to the children of men, hear the prayers of the faithful, and give power concerning those who have been destroyed. He loves the world, offers salvation freely, and commands repentance, charity, and righteous conduct.

l: the devil, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 26
s: The devil is the founder of secret combinations, murder, and works of darkness. He leads people gradually until he binds them with strong cords forever.

l: people of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 26
s: Nephi’s people will experience wars and contentions, and later many will dwindle in unbelief and be smitten by the Gentiles. After three generations and many of the fourth generation pass in righteousness, speedy destruction will come upon them.

l: Gentiles, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 26
s: The Gentiles will smite those who have dwindled in unbelief and will be lifted up in pride. They will build many churches, reject the power and miracles of God, preach their own wisdom for gain, and grind upon the poor.

l: prophets, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 26
s: Prophets will be cast out, stoned, and slain by the wicked. Those who heed the words of the prophets and do not destroy them will not perish.

l: saints, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 26
s: Saints will be persecuted, cast out, stoned, and slain. The cry of their blood will ascend to God, while those who protect them and look forward to Christ will be preserved.

l: the righteous, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 26
s: The righteous will heed the words of the prophets, endure persecution, and look forward to Christ with steadfastness. They will not perish, and the Son of righteousness will appear to and heal them.

l: the wicked, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 26
s: The wicked will perish because they cast out and kill prophets and saints. They will face fire, destruction, thunderings, lightnings, earthquakes, and other calamities, and will be consumed as stubble.

l: children of men, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 26
s: The children of men will receive signs, miracles, and teachings concerning Christ according to their faith. God invites all of them to come unto him and partake of his goodness.

l: those who have dwindled in unbelief, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 26
s: Those who have dwindled in unbelief will not be forgotten, and the words and prayers concerning them will be written and heard. They will be smitten by the Gentiles, and the destroyed among them will speak from the ground through a written and sealed book.

l: resurrection of Jesus Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 26
s: The resurrection of Christ will be followed by his showing himself to Nephi’s people. Signs will be given to the people concerning Christ’s birth, death, and resurrection.

l: destruction of the wicked, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 26
s: The destruction of the wicked will be great and terrible and will come through fire, earthquakes, storms, collapsing buildings, and other calamities. Those who choose darkness and yield to the devil will go down to hell.

l: the last days, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 26
s: The last days will include the dwindling and destruction of Nephi’s people, the rise of Gentile pride, many churches, secret combinations, and the bringing forth of written records. The words of the righteous and prayers of the faithful will still be preserved.

l: secret combinations, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 26
s: Secret combinations are described as existing according to the devil’s combinations. They are associated with murder and works of darkness.

l: priestcrafts, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 26
s: Priestcrafts occur when men preach and set themselves up as a light to the world to gain money and praise rather than seek the welfare of Zion. The Lord forbids priestcrafts.

l: salvation, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 26
s: Salvation is offered freely to all people, and none are forbidden from partaking of it. The Lord commands his people to persuade all men to repentance.

l: charity, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 26
s: Charity is love, and without it people are nothing. Those who have charity will not allow the laborer in Zion to perish.

l: unbelief, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 26
s: Unbelief will cause many of Nephi’s people to dwindle and be destroyed. Those who seek to destroy the things of God will not receive the written records concerning them.

l: pride, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 26
s: Pride will lead people to reap destruction and will cause the Gentiles to stumble. The proud who do wickedly will be burned up as stubble.

l: the secret works of darkness, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 26
s: Works of darkness are chosen over light by those who yield to the devil. They are associated with secret combinations and lead people to destruction.

l: the words of the prophets, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 26
s: The words of the prophets will guide the righteous, who heed them and look forward to Christ. The righteous’ words will be written, and their prayers will be heard.

l: The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: The unit concerns the Lord of Hosts, the Lord God, and God bringing forth a sealed book and its words to the children of men in the last days. The book contains a revelation from God, while its sealed words are withheld until the Lord’s due time, and its unsealed words are delivered by a man who receives the book and reads them. The nations, Gentiles, and Jews face visitation and destruction for iniquity and abominations, while Zion, the house of Jacob, the meek, and the poor are promised deliverance and understanding. The learned reject the book because of worldly motives, but God performs a marvelous work and a wonder through the man who reads the words and through witnesses.

l: Lord of Hosts, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: The Lord of Hosts visits the nations with thunder, earthquake, great noise, storm, tempest, and devouring fire. He knows the works of those who hide their counsel and promises that the terrible one, the scorner, and those who watch for iniquity will be brought to naught or cut off.

l: Lord God, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: The Lord God brings forth the words of a book, delivers the book and its words to a man, and establishes his word through witnesses. He directs the man who receives the book, preserves the sealed words, and shows that he can do his own work.

l: Jesus Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: God is able to do his own work and is a God of miracles. He shows the world that he is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and works among the children of men according to their faith.

l: Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: Christ provides the power by which the words of the book will be read and all things will be revealed to the children of men.

l: Holy One of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: The poor among men rejoice in the Holy One of Israel. The meek increase and have joy in the Lord.

l: Gentiles, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: The Gentiles, together with the Jews, become drunken with iniquity and all manner of abominations in the last days or days of the Gentiles. The nations of the Gentiles that fight against Zion are visited and become as a hungry or thirsty person whose dream leaves the soul empty.

l: Jews, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: The Jews, including those on this land and other lands, become drunken with iniquity and all manner of abominations. They are included among those who are visited by the Lord of Hosts.

l: nations, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: The nations of the earth become drunken with iniquity and abominations. Those that fight against Zion and distress her are visited, become as an empty dream, and are ultimately brought to naught or cut off.

l: Zion, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: Zion is fought against and distressed by the nations. Those nations are promised to become as a hungry or thirsty person whose dream leaves the soul empty.

l: Mount Zion, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: The multitude of all nations that fight against Mount Zion will become as an empty dream, like a hungry or thirsty person who awakens without satisfaction.

l: house of Jacob, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: The house of Jacob is told that Jacob shall no longer be ashamed or pale. When Jacob sees his children, they sanctify the name of the Holy One of Jacob and fear the God of Israel.

l: children of men, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: The children of men receive the words of the book and will eventually have all things revealed to them. The deaf hear the words of the book, the blind see out of obscurity and darkness, and those who erred in spirit come to understanding.

l: the learned, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: The learned ask to read the book for the glory of the world and to get gain, but they cannot read it because it is sealed. Their wisdom and understanding perish or are hidden because they reject the words.

l: man who receives the book, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: The man who receives the book delivers its unsealed words to another and is told to show them to the learned. He cannot bring the sealed book, and later receives the book and words again from the Lord God.

l: man who reads the words, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: The man who reads the words says that he is not learned. The Lord tells him to read the words given to him, not to touch the sealed things, and after obtaining the promised witnesses to seal and hide the book again.

l: three witnesses, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: Three witnesses behold the book by the power of God besides the man to whom it is delivered. They testify to the truth of the book and the things in it.

l: the book, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: The book contains words of those who have slumbered in the dust and a revelation from God from the beginning of the world to its ending. It is delivered to a man, hidden from the eyes of the world, and later sealed and hidden again.

l: sealed words, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: The sealed words are not delivered during the day of the wickedness and abominations of the people. They remain in the book until the Lord’s due time, when they will reveal all things from the foundation of the world to its end.

l: unsealed words, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: The unsealed words are delivered to another person to be shown to the learned. The man who is not learned is commanded to read the words that the Lord gives him.

l: revelation from God, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: The revelation from God in the book extends from the beginning of the world to its ending. The sealed revelation is kept in the book until the Lord’s due time.

l: word of the Holy One of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: The Lord God establishes his word through as many witnesses as seemeth him good. Woe is pronounced on anyone who rejects the word of God.

l: the last days, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: In the last days, or the days of the Gentiles, the nations of the Gentiles and the Jews become drunken with iniquity and abominations. The Lord then visits them and brings forth the words of the book.

l: visitation of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: The visitation of the Lord of Hosts comes with thunder, earthquake, great noise, storm, tempest, and devouring fire. It falls upon the nations that are drunken with iniquity and abominations.

l: destruction of nations fighting Zion, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: The nations fighting Zion and distressing her become as a dream of a night vision, like a hungry or thirsty person who awakens empty or faint. The terrible one, the scorner, and those watching for iniquity are also brought to naught or cut off.

l: the work of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: The Lord proceeds to do a marvelous work and a wonder among the people. Through it, the wisdom of the wise and learned perishes and the understanding of the prudent is hidden.

l: iniquity, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: Iniquity causes the nations, Gentiles, and Jews to become drunken and brings the Lord’s visitation. It also causes rulers and seers to be covered and leads people to hide their works from the Lord.

l: abominations, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: The people’s abominations contribute to the day when the sealed things are withheld from them. The nations, Gentiles, and Jews are drunken with all manner of abominations.

l: reading the book, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: Reading the book is given to a man who is not learned after the learned reject it. The words are read by the power of Christ, witnesses are obtained, and the book is then sealed and hidden again.

l: sealing and hiding the book, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 27
s: The book is sealed so that its revelation is kept until the Lord’s due time. After the man reads the commanded words and obtains the promised witnesses, he seals up the book again and hides it for the Lord to preserve the unread words.

l: The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: The Lord God warns the children of men about churches built up without Him, false doctrines, pride, wickedness, and denial of the Holy Ghost and the power of God. The devil deceives people through anger, carnal security, claims that there is no hell, and teachings that people have enough revelation. The Lord God calls for repentance, promises mercy, and teaches that He gives wisdom and revelation line upon line to those who heed His counsel. The great and abominable church and the kingdom of the devil will fall, while the humble followers of Christ may be led into error but remain distinct from the wicked.

l: Lord God, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: The Lord God warns of pride, false teachers, false doctrines, wickedness, and denial of His power. He promises mercy to those who repent and come unto Him, gives wisdom line upon line to those who heed His counsel, and will judge all according to their works.

l: Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: Jesus Christ is identified as the one whose humble followers remain among those who have not gone astray. The humble followers of Christ are nevertheless sometimes led into error because they are taught by the precepts of men.

l: Holy Ghost, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: The Holy Ghost gives utterance, and those who deny it are condemned. The text also teaches that precepts of men are acceptable only when given by the power of the Holy Ghost.

l: the devil, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: The devil stirs people to anger against that which is good, pacifies others into carnal security, flatters others by denying hell, and grasps people with everlasting chains. His deceptions lead souls carefully down to hell.

l: churches, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: Churches built up without the Lord contend with one another, teach by their learning, deny the Holy Ghost and the power of God, and become corrupted through pride, false teachers, and false doctrine. They are lifted up, rob the poor, and persecute the meek and poor in heart.

l: great and abominable church, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: The great and abominable church, called the whore of all the earth, must tumble to the earth, and its fall must be great.

l: the humble followers of Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: The humble followers of Christ are among the few who have not gone astray. Nevertheless, they are led into error in many instances because they are taught by the precepts of men.

l: children of men, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: The children of men will receive writings of great worth, especially the remnant of the house of Israel. The Lord God gives them wisdom and further knowledge line upon line when they receive His word and heed His counsel.

l: Gentiles, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: The Lord God lengthens His arm to the Gentiles from day to day, although they deny Him. He will be merciful to them if they repent and come unto Him.

l: inhabitants of the earth, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: The inhabitants of the earth will be destroyed when they are fully ripe in iniquity unless they repent of their wickedness and abominations.

l: Zion, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: Those who are at ease in Zion and cry that all is well are condemned. The claim that Zion prospers and all is well is presented as a deception that can lead souls to hell.

l: kingdom of God, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: Some falsely teach that God will justify a little sin and that people will eventually be saved in the kingdom of God. The text condemns this teaching as false, vain, and foolish.

l: hell, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: Hell is denied by some who claim there is no hell, but death, hell, the devil, and those seized by them must stand before the throne of God and be judged. The wicked are sent to a place prepared for them, a lake of fire and brimstone that is endless torment.

l: kingdom of the devil, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: The kingdom of the devil must shake, and those who belong to it must be stirred to repentance or be grasped by the devil's everlasting chains and perish.

l: miracles, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: Some teach that the Lord is no longer a God of miracles and that people should not believe in miracles wrought by His hand. This teaching is condemned as a denial of the power of God.

l: the power of God, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: Churches and teachers deny the power of God and teach that the Lord has given His power to men. Those who deny the power of God and the gift of the Holy Ghost are condemned.

l: word of the Holy One of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: Some claim that they have received the word of God and need no more, but the Lord God gives more to those who receive and takes away from those who say they have enough. He gives His word line upon line and precept upon precept.

l: precepts of men, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: Precepts of men lead churches and even the humble followers of Christ into error when they replace the Lord's counsel. They are acceptable only when given by the power of the Holy Ghost.

l: false doctrines, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: False doctrines are taught by people who are puffed up, seek to hide their counsels from the Lord, and work in darkness. False doctrines contribute to the corruption and lifting up of churches.

l: repentance, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: Repentance can prevent the inhabitants of the earth from being destroyed. The Lord God calls the Gentiles and those belonging to the kingdom of the devil to repent and come unto Him.

l: pride, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: Pride causes churches to become corrupted and lifted up, leads them to rob the poor and persecute the meek, and causes people to be puffed up in their hearts. Those who are wise, learned, or rich and puffed up in pride are condemned.

l: destruction of the wicked, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: The wicked will perish when they are fully ripe in iniquity, and those who follow false doctrines, commit whoredoms, or pervert the Lord's way will be thrust down to hell. Repentance can avert this destruction.

l: the fall of the great and abominable church, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 28
s: The fall of the great and abominable church will be great, and it must tumble to the earth.

l: The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 29
s: The Lord God declares that a marvelous work will recover the house of Israel and fulfill covenants and promises made to Nephi and his father. Gentiles are rebuked for rejecting additional scripture and for mistreating the Jews, from whom the Bible came. The Lord God teaches that he speaks to many nations, including the Jews, Nephites, lost tribes of Israel, and all nations, and that their written testimonies will be shared. The house of Israel will be gathered to the lands of its possessions, and the Lord God's word will be gathered into one.

l: Lord God, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 29
s: The Lord God declares that he remembers his covenants and people, speaks to all nations, and may give more scripture beyond the Bible. He will judge the world according to written works and show those who fight against his word and the house of Israel that he is God.

l: house of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 29
s: The house of Israel is the Lord God's people, whose recovery and gathering he promises. Its members will be gathered home to the lands of their possessions, and its written words will be gathered into one.

l: Jews, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 29
s: The Jews are described as the Lord God's ancient covenant people, from whom the Bible proceeds. They will receive and write the Lord God's words, and their words will be shared with the Nephites and the lost tribes of Israel.

l: Gentiles, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 29
s: The Gentiles are rebuked for saying that the Bible is sufficient, for failing to thank the Jews, and for cursing and hating them. They will receive more of the Lord God's word and will be judged for their treatment of the Jews.

l: Nephites, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 29
s: The Nephites are among the peoples to whom the Lord God will speak and who will write his words. They will have the words of the Jews and the lost tribes of Israel, and those peoples will have the words of the Nephites.

l: lost tribes of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 29
s: The lost tribes of Israel are among the tribes led away by the Lord God, and they will write the words he speaks to them. Their words will be shared with the Jews and Nephites.

l: Bible, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 29
s: The Bible proceeds from the Jews, the Lord God's ancient covenant people. Possessing a Bible does not mean that it contains all the Lord God's words or that no more scripture can be written.

l: word of the Holy One of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 29
s: The word of God will proceed to the ends of the earth as a standard for the house of Israel. The Lord God's words will be written by many peoples and eventually gathered in one.

l: the work of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 29
s: The marvelous work is a work the Lord God will undertake to remember his covenants and recover his people, including the house of Israel.

l: the covenants of the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 29
s: The Lord God remembers the covenants he made with the children of men and the ancient covenant people. He will fulfill his covenant with Abraham by remembering his seed forever.

l: nations, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 29
s: The Lord God teaches that there are many nations and that he creates and remembers all people, including those on the isles of the sea. He will speak to nations throughout the earth, and their written testimonies will serve as witnesses.

l: the gathering of Israel and Judah, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 29
s: The gathering of Israel includes the house of Israel being gathered home to the lands of its possessions. At that time, the Lord God's word will also be gathered in one.

l: The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 30
s: Nephi teaches that Gentiles who repent become covenant people, while Jews who do not repent are cast off, and he prophesies concerning both groups. The book will come forth among the Gentiles, and believers will carry its words to the remnant of Nephi’s seed, who will learn of their ancestry and Jesus Christ. The Lord God will restore his people, judge the wicked, and bring peace and righteousness to the earth. All things will be revealed to the children of men, and Satan will have power over their hearts no more for a long time.

l: Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 30
s: Nephi warns his beloved brethren not to suppose that they are more righteous than the Gentiles, because all who do not keep the commandments of God will perish. He prophesies concerning the Jews, the Gentiles, the remnant of his seed, and the Lord God’s future work.

l: Gentiles, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 30
s: The Gentiles are not utterly destroyed, and those who repent become the covenant people of the Lord. The book will come forth and be written unto them, and many of them will believe its words and carry them to the remnant of Nephi’s seed.

l: Jews, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 30
s: Jews who do not repent will be cast off, while scattered Jews will begin to believe in Christ and gather upon the face of the land. Those who believe in Christ will become a delightsome people.

l: the Lord, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 30
s: The Lord God will commence his work among all nations, kindreds, tongues, and people to restore his people upon the earth. He will judge the poor with righteousness, reprove the meek with equity, destroy the wicked, and bring about a time of peace.

l: Jesus Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 30
s: Jesus Christ is the Son of God and the Holy One of Israel. The remnant of Nephi’s seed will be restored to knowledge of Jesus Christ, and Jews who believe in Christ will become a delightsome people.

l: the seed of the speaker, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 30
s: The remnant of Nephi’s seed will learn that Nephi’s people came out from Jerusalem and that they are descendants of the Jews. The gospel of Jesus Christ will restore them to knowledge of their fathers and of Jesus Christ, and they will become a pure and delightsome people.

l: the book, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 30
s: The book of which Nephi has spoken will come forth, be written unto the Gentiles, and be sealed up again unto the Lord. Many will believe its words and carry them to the remnant of Nephi’s seed.

l: gospel of Jesus Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 30
s: The gospel of Jesus Christ will be declared among the remnant of Nephi’s seed. Through it, they will be restored to knowledge of their fathers and of Jesus Christ.

l: all nations, kindreds, tongues, and people, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 30
s: The Lord God will commence his work among all nations, kindreds, tongues, and people to bring about the restoration of his people upon the earth.

l: the earth, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 30
s: The Lord God will judge and divide the people upon the earth, destroy the wicked, and spare his people. The earth will be full of the knowledge of the Lord, and nothing will hurt or destroy in all the Lord’s holy mountain.

l: restoration of Israel, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 30
s: The restoration of his people upon the earth will be brought about through the Lord God’s work among all nations, kindreds, tongues, and people.

l: the wicked, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 30
s: The wicked will be destroyed when the Lord God causes a great division among the people. The Lord may destroy them by fire, and he will slay them with the breath of his lips.

l: the great division among the people, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 30
s: The great division among the people will come speedily when the Lord God separates the wicked from his people. The wicked will be destroyed, while the Lord will spare his people.

l: children of men, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 30
s: All things that have been revealed unto the children of men will be revealed at that day. There is nothing secret that will not be revealed, and nothing sealed upon the earth that will not be loosed.

l: Satan, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 30
s: Satan will have power over the hearts of the children of men no more for a long time.

l: The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 31
s: Nephi concludes his prophesying and teaches his beloved brethren plainly about the doctrine of Christ. He explains that Jesus Christ was baptized to fulfill all righteousness, and that people must repent, be baptized by water, receive the Holy Ghost, and endure to the end. He teaches that the way to eternal life requires pressing forward with faith in Christ, feasting upon the word of Christ, and relying on the merits of him who is mighty to save.

l: Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 31
s: Nephi makes an end of his prophesying and speaks plainly concerning the doctrine of Christ. He teaches that people must enter by repentance and baptism by water, receive the Holy Ghost, and endure to the end.

l: beloved brethren, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 31
s: Nephi addresses his beloved brethren and teaches them about the doctrine of Christ. He urges them to follow Jesus Christ, press forward with steadfastness, and endure to the end.

l: Lord God, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 31
s: The Lord God works among the children of men by giving light to their understanding and speaking according to their language and understanding.

l: Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 31
s: Jesus Christ is presented as the Lamb of God, the Son, the Lord, and the Savior. He was baptized by water to fulfill all righteousness, set an example, commanded people to follow him, and taught that those who endure to the end shall be saved.

l: God the Father, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 31
s: God the Father is witnessed to by those who are baptized and willing to keep his commandments. He gives the Holy Ghost to those baptized in the name of the Beloved Son and declares that those who endure to the end shall be saved.

l: Holy Ghost, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 31
s: The Holy Ghost descends upon Jesus Christ after his baptism in the form of a dove. It is received after baptism by water, brings the baptism of fire, witnesses of the Father and the Son, and enables people to speak with the tongue of angels.

l: children of men, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 31
s: The children of men are shown the example of Jesus Christ and the straightness of the path and narrowness of the gate. They are called to repent, be baptized, keep the commandments, follow Jesus Christ, and endure to the end.

l: commandments, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 31
s: The commandments of the Father are to be kept by those who follow Jesus Christ. Repentance, baptism, and willingness to keep the commandments are required in entering the way to eternal life.

l: repentance, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 31
s: Repentance is commanded by the Father and precedes baptism by water. It is part of the gate by which people enter the strait and narrow path.

l: baptism by water, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 31
s: Baptism by water is required even though Jesus Christ was holy, because he used it to fulfill all righteousness and show obedience to the Father. It is part of the gate by which people enter the strait and narrow path.

l: baptism of fire and of the Holy Ghost, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 31
s: The baptism of fire and of the Holy Ghost comes after repentance, baptism by water, and witnessing willingness to keep the commandments. It brings a new tongue and the ability to speak with the tongue of angels.

l: straight and narrow path, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 31
s: The straight and narrow path leads to eternal life. People enter it through the gate of repentance and baptism by water and must press forward, feast upon the word of Christ, and endure to the end.

l: gate, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 31
s: The gate by which people enter is repentance and baptism by water. After entering through the gate, they receive a remission of their sins by fire and by the Holy Ghost.

l: the doctrine of Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 31
s: The doctrine of Christ includes repentance, baptism by water, receiving the Holy Ghost, following Jesus Christ, and enduring to the end. Nephi identifies it as the only and true doctrine of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost.

l: words of Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 31
s: The word of Christ leads people into the way when they act with unshaken faith in him. People must feast upon it while pressing forward toward eternal life.

l: faith in Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 31
s: People enter the path through the word of Christ with unshaken faith in him. They must rely wholly upon the merits of him who is mighty to save.

l: enduring to the end, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 31
s: Those who endure to the end by following the example of the Son of the living God shall be saved. Enduring to the end is required after entering the strait and narrow path.

l: eternal life, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 31
s: Eternal life is promised to those who press forward with steadfastness in Christ, a perfect brightness of hope, and a love of God and all men while feasting upon the word of Christ and enduring to the end.

l: remission of sins, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 31
s: A remission of sins comes by fire and by the Holy Ghost after people enter through repentance and baptism by water.

l: The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 32
s: Nephi teaches his beloved brethren what they should do after entering in by the way. They should receive the Holy Ghost, feast upon the words of Christ, ask, knock, and pray always. The Holy Ghost reveals what they should do, while the words of Christ tell them all things necessary. Nephi says this is the doctrine of Christ and mourns the unbelief, wickedness, ignorance, and stiffneckedness of men.

l: Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 32
s: Nephi teaches his beloved brethren to receive the Holy Ghost, feast upon the words of Christ, ask, knock, and pray always. He cannot say more because the Spirit stoppeth his utterance, and he is left to mourn because of men's unbelief, wickedness, ignorance, and stiffneckedness.

l: beloved brethren, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 32
s: The beloved brethren ponder what they should do after entering in by the way. They are taught to receive the Holy Ghost, feast upon the words of Christ, seek knowledge, and pray.

l: straight and narrow path, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 32
s: After entering in by the way, people should receive the Holy Ghost. If they enter in by the way and receive the Holy Ghost, it will show them all things they should do.

l: Holy Ghost, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 32
s: The Holy Ghost enables people to speak with the tongue of angels and shows them all things they should do. It is received after entering in by the way.

l: angels, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 32
s: Angels speak by the power of the Holy Ghost. They speak the words of Christ.

l: Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 32
s: Christ's words tell people all things they should do. He will manifest himself in the flesh, and people should observe the things he says to do.

l: words of Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 32
s: The words of Christ should be feasted upon. They tell people all things they should do.

l: the doctrine of Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 32
s: The doctrine of Christ includes entering in by the way and receiving the Holy Ghost. No more doctrine will be given until Christ manifests himself in the flesh.

l: the Spirit, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 32
s: The Spirit stoppeth Nephi's utterance. The Spirit teaches a man to pray.

l: men, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 32
s: Men will not search knowledge or understand great knowledge when it is given to them in plainness. Nephi mourns their unbelief, wickedness, ignorance, and stiffneckedness.

l: prayer, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 32
s: People must pray always and not faint. They must pray unto the Father in the name of Christ before performing anything unto the Lord, so that their performance may be for the welfare of their soul.

l: God the Father, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 32
s: People should pray unto the Father in the name of Christ before performing anything unto the Lord. They ask that he consecrate their performance for the welfare of their soul.

l: The Second Book of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 33
s: Nephi says he cannot write everything taught among his people and that his written words, though weak, have great worth because they teach about Jesus Christ and persuade people to do good, believe in him, and endure to the end. He prays continually for his people and knows that God will consecrate his prayers for their gain. Nephi teaches that Jews, Gentiles, and all people must be reconciled to Christ, enter the narrow gate, and continue in the strait path until the end of the day of probation. He warns that Christ will confirm the words at the final judgment and that those who reject the goodness of God and these words will be condemned.

l: Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 33
s: Nephi says he cannot write all that was taught among his people and that he is not mighty in writing as he is in speaking. He writes for the benefit of his people, prays for them, teaches about Christ, and says he must obey what the Lord commanded him to write.

l: Holy Ghost, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 33
s: The Holy Ghost carries spoken words unto the hearts of the children of men. Some harden their hearts against the Holy Ghost, leaving it no place in them.

l: Lord God, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 33
s: Nephi cries unto God in faith and knows that God will hear his cry. He says the Lord God will consecrate his prayers for the gain of his people.

l: Jesus Christ, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 33
s: Jesus Christ is spoken of in Nephi's writing, which persuades people to believe in him and endure to the end. People must be reconciled unto Christ, and Christ will show at the last day that the words are his.

l: people of Nephi, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 33
s: Nephi prays continually for his people because he has charity for them. His written words are intended especially for them and are meant to persuade them to do good.

l: Jews, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 33
s: Nephi says he has charity for the Jew because he means those from whence he came. He says people must respect the words of the Jews.

l: Gentiles, The Second Book of Nephi, Chapter 33
s: Nephi says he has charity for the Gentiles. He says he cannot hope for them unless they are reconciled unto Christ and continue in the path until the end of the day of probation.
